title: The ladder
description: Section five: what the invested balance buys back, in three groups. An item has a fixed price or a priceFrom block, never both. Every rung is ONE indivisible thing; the site multiplies it. Never price a rung as a bundle of N things, or the plural becomes a tally of sets: 'Sets of three paid-off homes'. If you want three homes, price one home and let the count say 3x.

groups.description: Rendered in this order. Each group is its own price-ordered ladder.

lede.description: One line under the group title.

includesCharity.description: When true, every item in charity.json joins this group and is priced in alongside its rungs. Exactly one group must set this, or charity.json renders nowhere.

footnote.description: Caveat printed under this group's rungs. Use it where the prices need a warning the notes section cannot carry.

group.description: Must name a group above. Groups are about who the rung is for, not what it costs.

singular.description: One of the thing. Not a bundle of several.

plural.description: Read it aloud after a number: "27x Used cars, owned outright". If it only makes sense as a set, the rung is priced wrong.

singularInState.description: Used when a real state is picked. Supports the {state} token.

ref.description: Where the price comes from. A reader.* ref prices the rung from the reader's own take-home; use a fractional multiplier for less than a year. Add a case to src/lib/ladder.ts before adding a value here.

note.description: Shown under the label. Supports the {price} token.
